<th class="tl" colspan="1" rowspan="2"><div style="width: 200px;"><strong>Conversion from IFRS to GAAP<br></strong></div></th>
<th class="th" colspan="1">12 Months Ended</th>
</tr>
<tr><th class="th"><div>Dec. 31, 2025</div></th></tr>
<tr class="re">
<td class="pl" style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="Show.showAR( this, 'defref_LEEF_DisclosureConversionFromIfrsToGaapAbstract', window );"><strong>Conversion From Ifrs To Gaap</strong></a></td>
<td class="text">&#160;<span></span>
</td>
</tr>
<tr class="ro">
<td class="pl custom" style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="Show.showAR( this, 'defref_LEEF_ConversionFromIfrsToGaapTextBlock', window );">Conversion from IFRS to GAAP</a></td>
<td class="text"><p id="xdx_809_ecustom--ConversionFromIfrsToGaapTextBlock_z2VAHW7EubS2" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; font-size: 10pt">
  <tr style="vertical-align: top">
    <td style="width: 30px"><span style="font-size: 10pt"><b>4.</b></span></td>
    <td style="text-align: justify"><span style="font-size: 10pt"><b><span id="xdx_827_z35JaLUHbP34">Conversion from IFRS to GAAP</span></b></span></td></tr>
  </table>
<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><b>&#160;</b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The Company has retrospectively converted its
Consolidated Financial Statements from International Financial Reporting Standards (&#8220;IFRS&#8221;) to GAAP.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The significant differences between IFRS and
GAAP as they related to these financial statements are as follows:</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; font-size: 10pt">
  <tr style="vertical-align: top">
    <td style="width: 24px"><span style="font-size: 10pt"><b>(a)</b></span></td>
    <td style="text-align: justify"><span style="font-size: 10pt"><b>Leases</b></span></td></tr>
  </table>
<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><b>&#160;</b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">Under IFRS, prior to the adoption
of GAAP, the Company, as lessee, applied the single lease model that is similar to the accounting for a finance lease under GAAP. The
expense recognition presented a higher portion of the total expense earlier in the term as a combination of straight-line depreciation
of the right-of-use asset and the effective interest rate method applied to the lease liability results in a decreasing rate of interest
expense recognition throughout the lease term.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">Under GAAP, there is dual classification
lease accounting model for lessees: finance leases and operating leases. The Company, as lessee, classified all its leases as operating
leases and recognizes a single lease expense, including both a right-of-use asset depreciation component and an interest component, on
a straight-line basis throughout the term. This resulted in lease expense being reclassified from interest expense into operating expense
under GAAP which decreased interest expense by $<span id="xdx_901_eus-gaap--IncreaseDecreaseInPrepaidInterest_c20230101__20231231_zHEYk481SFuf" title="Interest expense">467,889</span> for the year ended December 31, 2023. Additionally, due to the change in the
expense recognition method, the total resulting decrease in lease related expense from the transition from IFRS to GAAP was $<span id="xdx_90A_eus-gaap--LeaseCost_c20230101__20231231_zU7UyJifU5nf" title="Lease cost">200,177</span>
for the year ended December 31, 2023.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">Additionally, under GAAP, the right-of-use
asset is reported separately on the consolidated balance sheet from property and equipment. Accordingly, this balance was split out separately
as of December 31, 2023.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; font-size: 10pt">
  <tr style="vertical-align: top">
    <td style="width: 24px"><span style="font-size: 10pt"><b>(b)</b></span></td>
    <td style="text-align: justify"><span style="font-size: 10pt"><b>Notes Payable</b></span></td></tr>
  </table>
<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><b>&#160;</b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">On May 25, 2023, the Company entered
into a Loan Agreement with ADSB for a total of $<span id="xdx_908_eus-gaap--NotesPayable_iI_c20230525__us-gaap--TypeOfArrangementAxis__custom--LoanAgreementMember__dei--LegalEntityAxis__custom--AndersonDevelopmentSBLLCMember_zvkSBmGWsrXh" title="Notes payable">7,000,000</span> which is zero-interest bearing. The loan was issued in connection with <span id="xdx_90C_eus-gaap--ClassOfWarrantOrRightOutstanding_iI_c20230525__us-gaap--TypeOfArrangementAxis__custom--LoanAgreementMember__dei--LegalEntityAxis__custom--AndersonDevelopmentSBLLCMember_zfA1HchwSWJ4" title="Detached warrants">5,687,500</span>
detached warrants which are immediately exercisable at a price of CAD$<span id="xdx_90A_eus-gaap--ClassOfWarrantOrRightExercisePriceOfWarrantsOrRights1_iI_pid_uCADPShares_c20230525__us-gaap--TypeOfArrangementAxis__custom--LoanAgreementMember__dei--LegalEntityAxis__custom--AndersonDevelopmentSBLLCMember_zwG2SXMqk0a2" title="Exercisable price">0.80</span> per share (USD $<span id="xdx_906_eus-gaap--ClassOfWarrantOrRightExercisePriceOfWarrantsOrRights1_iI_pid_c20230525__us-gaap--TypeOfArrangementAxis__custom--LoanAgreementMember__dei--LegalEntityAxis__custom--AndersonDevelopmentSBLLCMember_zfE6jMEZtuS6" title="Exercisable price">0.60</span>) for a period of 60 months from the date
of issuance. Upon full repayment of the loan the Company will transfer <span id="xdx_903_eus-gaap--RepaymentsOfDebt_c20230525__20230525__us-gaap--TypeOfArrangementAxis__custom--LoanAgreementMember__dei--LegalEntityAxis__custom--AndersonDevelopmentSBLLCMember__us-gaap--StatementClassOfStockAxis__custom--ClassAUnitsMember__srt--TitleOfIndividualAxis__custom--LenderMember_zrKMVRXGL6a1" title="Repayment of loans">720,000</span> Class A Units of ADSB to the lender. Under IFRS, the repayment
provisions of the loan contained sufficient uncertainty such that neither the warrants nor the ADSB transfer were determined to create
a debt discount against the note.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">Under GAAP, both the warrants and
the ADSB transfer were determined to create a debt discount totaling $<span id="xdx_904_eus-gaap--DebtInstrumentUnamortizedDiscount_iI_c20230525__us-gaap--TypeOfArrangementAxis__custom--LoanAgreementMember__dei--LegalEntityAxis__custom--AndersonDevelopmentSBLLCMember_zZfH3C4RoZFk" title="Debt discount">3,809,659</span> that is amortized over the term of the loan. During the
year ended December 31, 2023, amortization of the debt discount of $<span id="xdx_906_eus-gaap--AmortizationOfDebtDiscountPremium_c20230101__20231231__us-gaap--TypeOfArrangementAxis__custom--LoanAgreementMember__dei--LegalEntityAxis__custom--AndersonDevelopmentSBLLCMember_zrnSh45nxHj9" title="Amortization of debt discount">662,549</span> was recorded.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; font-size: 10pt">
  <tr style="vertical-align: top">
    <td style="width: 24px"><span style="font-size: 10pt"><b>(c)</b></span></td>
    <td style="text-align: justify"><span style="font-size: 10pt"><b>Warrants</b></span></td></tr>
  </table>
<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><b>&#160;</b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">During 2023, the Company issued warrants
to purchase the Company&#8217;s common stock for a total of <span id="xdx_908_eus-gaap--ClassOfWarrantOrRightNumberOfSecuritiesCalledByEachWarrantOrRight_iI_c20231231__us-gaap--StatementEquityComponentsAxis__us-gaap--WarrantMember_zKE1Ezlqckz1" title="Warrants to purchase common stock">6,462,898</span> shares. Under IFRS, these warrants were accounted for by recording
stock based compensation of $<span id="xdx_90C_eus-gaap--EmployeeBenefitsAndShareBasedCompensationNoncash_c20230101__20231231__us-gaap--StatementEquityComponentsAxis__us-gaap--WarrantMember_zny8dhmgJ68e" title="Share based compensation">957,517</span>. Due to the warrants being exercisable in a currency other than the Company&#8217;s functional currency,
under GAAP, these warrants were accounted for as a derivative liability to be recorded at fair value upon issuance and adjusted to fair
value at each reporting date. Accordingly, stock based compensation for the year ended December 31, 2023 was reduced by $<span id="xdx_904_eus-gaap--EmployeeBenefitsAndShareBasedCompensationNoncash_c20230101__20231231__us-gaap--StatementEquityComponentsAxis__us-gaap--WarrantMember_zsWbc1XLbsb6" title="Share based compensation">957,517</span> and
a derivative liability of $<span id="xdx_907_eus-gaap--DerivativeLiabilities_iI_c20231231__us-gaap--StatementEquityComponentsAxis__us-gaap--WarrantMember_zUlWpr9p3egc" title="Change in fair value derivative liability">946,649</span> was established as of December 31, 2023.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"></p>



<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; font-size: 10pt">
  <tr style="vertical-align: top">
    <td style="width: 24px"><span style="font-size: 10pt"><b>(d)</b></span></td>
    <td style="text-align: justify"><span style="font-size: 10pt"><b>Amortization of Intangible Assets</b></span></td></tr>
  </table>
<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><b>&#160;</b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">Under IFRS, the tradename and license
intangible assets acquired in connection with the acquisition of The Leaf in January 2023 (see Note 8) were determined to have an indefinite
life and were not subject to amortization. Under GAAP, these intangible assets were determined to have a definite life, which was determined
to be a useful life of <span id="xdx_907_eus-gaap--FiniteLivedIntangibleAssetUsefulLife_iI_pid_dtY_c20231231_zsfGl27OT7pc" title="Amortization of intangible assets use full life in years">10</span> years. Accordingly, intangible amortization for the year ended December 31, 2023 of $<span id="xdx_90A_eus-gaap--AmortizationOfIntangibleAssets_c20230101__20231231_zsWis10vIqZe" title="Amortization of intangible assets">339,000</span> was recorded.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; font-size: 10pt">
  <tr style="vertical-align: top">
    <td style="width: 24px"><span style="font-size: 10pt"><b>(e)</b></span></td>
    <td style="text-align: justify"><span style="font-size: 10pt"><b>Income Taxes</b></span></td></tr>
  </table>
<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><b>&#160;</b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">Prior to the adoption of GAAP, the
Company accounted for income taxes pursuant to International Accounting Standard 12, Income Taxes (&#8220;IAS 12&#8221;), International
Financial Reporting Interpretations Committee 23, Uncertainty over Income Tax Treatments (&#8220;IFRIC 23&#8221;), and International
Accounting Standard 34, Interim Reporting (&#8220;IAS 34&#8221;). Upon the adoption of GAAP, the Company now accounts for income taxes
pursuant to Accounting Standards Codification 740, Income Taxes (&#8220;ASC 740&#8221;) as noted below:</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; font-size: 10pt">
  <tr style="vertical-align: top">
    <td style="width: 48px">&#160;</td>
    <td style="width: 48px"><span style="font-size: 10pt">(i)</span></td>
    <td style="text-align: justify"><span style="font-size: 10pt">Deferred Tax</span></td></tr>
  </table>
<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">Deferred tax has been adjusted to remove
any backwards tracing components that are permitted under IAS 12 and prohibited under ASC 740. Specifically, backwards tracing is prohibited
with regard to adjustments to the beginning of the year balance of a valuation allowance because of a change in judgment about the realizability
of related deferred tax assets in future years.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; font-size: 10pt">
  <tr style="vertical-align: top">
    <td style="width: 48px">&#160;</td>
    <td style="width: 48px"><span style="font-size: 10pt">(ii)</span></td>
    <td style="text-align: justify"><span style="font-size: 10pt">Valuation Allowance</span></td></tr>
  </table>
<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">The realizability of deferred tax assets
was considered under GAAP and the determination to maintain a full valuation allowance in the United States was made. This is a substantially
similar result under IFRS. For footnote presentation purposes, all deferred tax assets, liabilities, and valuation allowances are now
reported on a gross basis rather than a net basis.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; font-size: 10pt">
  <tr style="vertical-align: top">
    <td style="width: 48px">&#160;</td>
    <td style="width: 48px"><span style="font-size: 10pt">(iii)</span></td>
    <td style="text-align: justify"><span style="font-size: 10pt">Uncertain Tax Positions</span></td></tr>
  </table>
<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">The Company recognizes and measures any
uncertain tax positions in accordance with ASC 740 rather than IFRIC 23. Accordingly, the Company recognizes and measures uncertain tax
positions based on a two-step process outlined in the Income Tax section of the Significant Accounting Policies.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; font-size: 10pt">
  <tr style="vertical-align: top">
    <td style="width: 48px">&#160;</td>
    <td style="width: 48px"><span style="font-size: 10pt">(iv)</span></td>
    <td style="text-align: justify"><span style="font-size: 10pt">Stock Based Compensation</span></td></tr>
  </table>
<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">Under IFRS, the measurement of the stock-based
compensation deferred tax asset is based on an estimate of the future tax deduction based on the current stock price at each reporting
period. When the expected tax benefits from equity awards exceed the recorded cumulative recognized expense multiplied by the tax rate,
the tax benefit up to the amount of the tax effect of the cumulative book compensation expense is recorded in the consolidated statement
of operations and comprehensive income (loss); the excess is recorded in equity. When the expected tax benefit is less than the tax effect
of the cumulative amount of recognized expense, the entire tax benefit is recorded in the consolidated statement of operations and comprehensive
income (loss).</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">Under GAAP, the Company measures the
stock-based compensation deferred tax asset based on the amount of compensation cost recognized for financial statement purposes. Changes
in stock price do not result in a remeasurement of the related deferred tax asset. Upon settlement of expiration, excess tax benefits
and tax deficiencies are recognized within the provisions for income taxes.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; font-size: 10pt">
  <tr style="vertical-align: top">
    <td style="width: 48px">&#160;</td>
    <td style="width: 48px"><span style="font-size: 10pt">(v)</span></td>
    <td style="text-align: justify"><span style="font-size: 10pt">Other Pre-tax Changes</span></td></tr>
  </table>
<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">The tax effects resulting from other
accounting changes to pre-tax income are included in the tax provision under GAAP.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"></p>



<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p id="xdx_898_ecustom--ScheduleOfReconciliationBetweenIFRSNetLossAndGAAPNetLossTableTextBlock_zy3kaUn6HXr7" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The reconciliation between IFRS net loss and
GAAP net loss for the year ended December 31, 2023 in the Company&#8217;s consolidated statements of operations and comprehensive income
(loss) is as follows:</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><span style="display: none; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#160;<span id="xdx_8B7_znJwRIzul6d4">Schedule

  <tr style="vertical-align: bottom; background-color: rgb(204,238,255)">
